the glyoxylate reductases (GLYRs) are a highly conserved group of enzymes with important roles in plant growth and development.

the glyoxylate reductase activity of GLYR1 was found to be important for the reduction of glyoxylate in the cytosol under chilling stress, whereas the succinic semialde-hyde reductase activity was found to be of importance for the reduction of succinic semial-dehyde in the plastid and mitochondria under chilling stress.

plant glyoxylate reductases (GLYRs) have been found in all plant species investigated so far and have been implicated to be involved in a number of stress responses, including chilling.
the plant GLYRs are not only important for plant growth and development, but are also crucial for the response to chilling stress.
